historical_claims.anchor: Section 8 of the Davis–Kahan paper resolves this for an important class of perturbations, those that only couple a subspace to its complement.
Davis and Kahan call this spectral repulsion.

related_resources.reason: Schur complements, used to show that an off-diagonal coupling cannot put spectrum into an ordered gap.
Second-order eigenvalue shifts versus first-order eigenvector rotation under off-diagonal coupling.
Quadratic-form inequalities such as A1 - alpha <= C1 (Lambda1 - alpha) C1.

description: Analyzes strictly off-diagonal self-adjoint perturbations, the continuation of the intended spectral branch below a 45-degree angle, and the eigenvalue repulsion that strengthens angle estimates; distinguishes the selected branch from arbitrary spectral subspaces.
